remarks: The apparent primary Directorate-of-Factories portal, tsfactories.cgg.gov.in, was completely unreachable this session (TLS reset on every attempt, 8 tries across several minutes with retries and delays). Given the spec's rule to exclude rather than include on doubt, nothing from that host is in verifiedSources even though search snippets strongly suggest it hosts the consolidated Telangana Factories Rules, 1950 PDF and the official Acts/GOs/Circulars listing. A future session with different network access should re-attempt this host specifically, since it is likely the single most important source for this service and is currently missing from the verified list.

labour.telangana.gov.in (Dept. of Labour, Employment, Training & Factories) is actively blocked by an F5 WAF for this fetch method/session (HTTP 403), so it could not be verified either, despite appearing to host department-level information.

Several ipass.telangana.gov.in fetches (Downloads.aspx, Checklist.aspx) returned a transient TLS 'Connection reset by peer' on the first attempt and succeeded on retry (HTTP 200) within the same session — these were verified on the successful retry, consistent with the spec's guidance to actually confirm resolution, not just note the first failure.

services.india.gov.in is blocked outright by this session's egress proxy policy (502 on CONNECT), so several Telangana-specific service-detail pages listed there (grant of manufacturer's licence, annual licence fee payment, change of occupier, etc.) could not be attempted at all, not just failed verification.

No separate NSWS state/service-specific deep link for Telangana factory licence could be verified (NSWS approvals for a given service typically sit behind login); only the general NSWS home page was confirmed. It is included because TG-iPASS itself surfaces NSWS as an integrated channel (About NSWS / Approvals List / Login in its own menu).

Excluded dca.telangana.gov.in manufacturing-licence checklist PDFs and GHMC industrial-GO PDFs found in search results were not tested/listed at all (not merely excluded) because on inspection they concern drug-manufacturing licensing and municipal/industrial-policy GOs respectively, not the Factories Act Factory License (FAL) process, so they were judged out of scope rather than failed candidates.
